RUMBLE THEME TOKEN REFERENCE
============================

Companion to blank-theme.rumble-theme. Fill that file in, save it under a new
name, then load it with File > Import Theme (the dialog filters for
*.rumble-theme, but any .json works too). An imported theme is copied into
custom_themes.json in your data dir and appears in Settings > Appearance
alongside the built-ins.

A theme is a flat JSON object. Nothing is nested, and unknown keys are ignored.


FORMAT RULES
------------
Colours       "#RRGGBB" or "#RRGGBBAA" (6 or 8 hex digits, with the leading #).
              Nothing else is accepted -- no 3-digit shorthand, no "red", no
              rgb(). Case does not matter. The AA byte is straight alpha:
              00 = fully transparent, FF = opaque. Only the four tokens marked
              (alpha) below are normally given one, but any colour may carry it.

Levers        Plain JSON numbers (no quotes). 1.0 is the engine's baseline.

name          The theme's display name. Must be filled in and must NOT collide
              with a built-in (Soundwave, Panther, Malice, Prime, Screamer,
              Bludgeon, Sage, System) or the import is rejected.

accent_name   Free-text label for the accent colour ("Cyan", "Signal Red").
              Cosmetic only -- it is never parsed.

Missing colour tokens are silently backfilled from Soundwave's values (the
fallback theme), so a half-filled file still imports. That is a safety net, not
a plan: a theme with a bright accent and Soundwave's dark navy surfaces
backfilled underneath will look like a bug. Fill everything in.


BACKGROUNDS -- the surface ladder, darkest to nearest
-----------------------------------------------------
bg_deep       The layer behind everything: window backdrop, empty space.
bg_sunken     Recessed surfaces -- text fields, combo boxes, spin boxes.
bg_base       The default panel background; also the scrollbar groove.
bg_surface    Cards, list rows, menus -- one step above the panel.
bg_raised     The nearest layer: hovered rows, popups, elevated chips.

Keep these ordered by lightness (each a visible step from the last, none of them
big jumps). A dark theme runs near-black upward; a light theme runs light-grey
upward to near-white. If two adjacent steps are too close the UI reads flat; if
they are too far apart it reads like mismatched patches.


BORDERS
-------
border_subtle    Hairlines you should barely notice -- dividers, card edges.
border_default   The normal visible outline on inputs and buttons.
border_strong    The focus/selection outline. Usually the accent itself.


ACCENT
------
accent           The one colour that carries the theme's identity: primary
                 buttons, the EQ curve, active states, links.
accent_hover     Accent lightened for hover. Built-ins go roughly 15-20% lighter.
accent_active    Accent darkened for the pressed state, roughly 15-20% darker.
accent_muted     (alpha) Accent at ~15% for selection fills and chip backgrounds.
                 Built-ins use the accent hex + "26" (0x26 = 38/255 = 15%).
accent_glow      (alpha) Accent at ~33% for focus halos. Built-ins append "55".


TEXT
----
text_primary     Body and heading text. This is the contrast that matters most:
                 aim for a strong ratio against bg_surface, not just bg_deep.
text_secondary   Sub-labels, less important values.
text_muted       Placeholders, disabled text, hints.
text_on_accent   Text drawn ON an accent fill (e.g. the Save button's label).
                 Pick by the accent's brightness: near-black on a light accent,
                 white on a dark one. Getting this backwards is the single most
                 common way a custom theme ends up unreadable.


SEMANTIC
--------
success          Confirmations, healthy state.
warning          Cautions.
error            Failures, clipping, destructive actions.
info             Informational banners.

Each built-in draws these from its own character palette rather than sharing one
semantic set, so they are NOT identical across themes. Keep the meanings legible
anyway: a green-ish success and a warm warning cost the user nothing, whereas a
red warning next to a red error leaves them unable to tell the two apart. Where
a palette had no usable colour for a state (no green for success, no amber for
warning), the built-ins keep a sane semantic colour rather than force the
palette. Whatever you pick, make sure it is actually visible on your surfaces --
an alert nobody can see is worse than an off-brand one.


EQ GRAPH
--------
graph_bg         The plot's own background -- typically a shade darker (or, on a
                 light theme, lighter) than bg_base so the graph reads inset.
graph_grid       Grid lines. Low contrast; they must never compete with the curve.
graph_zero       The 0 dB line. A step stronger than the grid.
graph_curve      The response curve. Almost always the accent.
graph_band       (alpha) Fill of a filter's band region. Built-ins: accent + "26".
graph_band_sel   The SELECTED band -- must contrast against graph_curve/accent,
                 so pick a complementary hue, not another shade of the accent.
graph_handle     The draggable filter handles. Usually the accent.
graph_text       Axis labels and tick numbers.

graph_points     Optional. Node markers. Falls back to graph_band_sel.
graph_geq        Optional. The GraphicEQ curve. Falls back to graph_band_sel.
graph_ir         Optional. The convolution/impulse-response curve. Falls back to
                 graph_points, then graph_band_sel.

Those three fall back rather than fail, but the fallbacks collapse distinct
curves onto one colour -- set them if your theme shows GEQ or IR profiles.


SCROLLBARS
----------
scrollbar_track        The groove. Built-ins reuse bg_base.
scrollbar_thumb        The bar. Built-ins reuse border_default.
scrollbar_thumb_hover  The bar under the cursor. Built-ins blend the thumb ~40%
                       toward the accent.


STRUCTURAL LEVERS -- shape and material, not colour
---------------------------------------------------
All five are optional numbers. Omit them and the engine uses its neutral
baseline (1.0, and 0.90 for glass_alpha). They are what stop two themes with
different palettes from feeling like the same UI recoloured.

radius_scale   Corner roundness, as a multiplier on the base radii.
               Built-in range: 0.6 (Panther, sharp stealth) to 1.2 (Malice,
               rounded). 1.0 is standard.

sheen          Gradient gloss on buttons and surfaces.
               Built-in range: 0.7 (Panther, flat matte) to 1.3 (Bludgeon,
               glossy). Higher = wetter, more reflective.

bevel          Strength of the raised light edge on surfaces.
               Built-in range: 0.8 (Panther) to 1.2 (Bludgeon). Higher =
               harder, more machined edges.

glow           Intensity of the accent glow and elevation drop-shadows.
               Built-in range: 0.2 (Panther, stealth matte) to 1.2 (Malice,
               glowy). 0 kills the glow entirely.

glass_alpha    Opacity of the translucent "glass" panel fills, 0.0-1.0.
               Built-in range: 0.87 (Soundwave, most see-through) to 0.95
               (Panther, nearly solid). Low values let the backdrop gradient
               show through the chrome; too low and text loses its ground.


WHERE YOUR THEME LANDS IN THE PICKER
------------------------------------
You do not choose its position. Settings > Appearance and the tray menu sort
every theme -- built-in, custom and imported alike -- by colour family (black,
blue, indigo, violet, red, pink, orange, green, teal, yellow, white) and then by
brightness within that family. The family comes from your accent's hue angle,
except that any theme whose bg_base is brighter than 50% luminance is filed
under "white" no matter what its accent is. A desaturated (grey/metal) accent on
a very dark theme files under "black".


A WORKED EXAMPLE: A NEUTRAL GRAPHITE THEME
------------------------------------------
Pure monochrome graphite on true OLED black; stealth-matte, lightly squared.
A neutral starting point if the blank file is too abstract (it is not one of
the shipped built-ins, so the name is free to reuse). This is the object BODY,
not a whole file -- paste it between the { and } of blank-theme.rumble-theme
(two tokens per line here purely to keep it readable; JSON does not care).

  "name": "My Theme",              "accent_name": "Graphite",

  "bg_deep": "#000000",            "bg_sunken": "#030304",
  "bg_base": "#070708",            "bg_surface": "#0D0D0F",
  "bg_raised": "#151517",

  "border_subtle": "#161618",      "border_default": "#26262B",
  "border_strong": "#737B8B",

  "accent": "#737B8B",             "accent_hover": "#8E96A6",
  "accent_active": "#565D6B",      "accent_muted": "#737B8B26",
  "accent_glow": "#737B8B55",

  "text_primary": "#ECECF3",       "text_secondary": "#8C8C9E",
  "text_muted": "#4C4C58",         "text_on_accent": "#FFFFFF",

  "success": "#2BD4A0",            "warning": "#FFB13C",
  "error": "#FF5C66",              "info": "#737B8B",

  "graph_bg": "#040405",           "graph_grid": "#101017",
  "graph_zero": "#242432",         "graph_curve": "#737B8B",
  "graph_band": "#737B8B55",       "graph_band_sel": "#FFB13C",
  "graph_handle": "#737B8B",       "graph_text": "#34343F",
  "graph_points": "#5F93FF",

  "scrollbar_track": "#070708",    "scrollbar_thumb": "#26262B",
  "scrollbar_thumb_hover": "#454851",

  "radius_scale": 0.7,             "sheen": 0.8,
  "bevel": 1.0,                    "glow": 0.3,
  "glass_alpha": 0.97


TWO OTHER WAYS TO BUILD A THEME
-------------------------------
Settings > Theme Creator edits every colour token live with swatch pickers,
starting from any built-in. It cannot set the five structural levers -- for
those, edit the JSON.

File > Export Current Theme writes whichever theme is active out as a complete
.rumble-theme file. Exporting a built-in gives you a filled-in file to modify,
which is often faster than starting from blank (just change "name" first, or
the import will refuse it as a built-in collision).
